item.title: Exclusive: Pain Care Startup Zanskar In Talks To Raise $6 Mn In Round Led By Bessemer
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Delhi NCR-based pain care startup Zanskar is in talks to raise about $6 Mn in a fresh funding round led…
item.content:encoded:
Delhi NCR-based pain care startup Zanskar is in talks to raise about $6 Mn in a fresh funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, sources told Inc42. 

The discussions are ongoing and final cheque size could change before the round is closed, the sources added. 

Zanskar and Bessemer Venture Partners did not respond to Inc42’s queries till the time of publication. 

The development comes about 10 months after the startup raised ₹2.8 Cr in a seed funding round led by Zeropearl VC, with participation from angel investors including Fashinza cofounder Pawan Gupta, 10X Growth Ventures managing partner Amit Baid, and Oaktree Capital SVP Nidhish Mundra. 

Founded in 2022 by IIT Delhi alumni Anshul Mittal and Manu Kumar Mittal, Zanskar operates a technology-led pain management platform offering personalised at-home care protocols through its app. It also sells pain relief products, including oils, roll-ons, and nutritional supplements, through its website and ecommerce platforms such as Blinkit, Tata 1mg, Amazon, and Flipkart. 

Earlier, the startup said it was exploring pilots for physiotherapy-led wellness centres in select metro cities as part of its broader pain management ecosystem. 

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in startups tackling chronic pain management. Earlier this year, Nivaan Care raised $7 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Sorin Investments with participation from W Health Ventures and other investors. Last year, FlexifyMe secured ₹20 Cr in a pre-Series A round to expand its online physiotherapy platform for chronic pain management. 

According to a report, nearly 47% of Indians aged 45 and above experience joint pain, while about 31% suffer from persistent back pain. The report added that untreated chronic pain and prolonged dependence on painkillers can lead to disability and other serious health complications. 

According to Inc42’s ‘Annual Indian Startup Trends Report, 2025’, the market for healthtech is projected to grow at 39% CAGR from 2025 to cross the $37 Bn+ mark by 2030. However, funding activity remained muted, with the number of deals falling to 54 in 2025 from 78 a year earlier.

item.title: Exclusive: AC Maker Optimist In Talks To Raise $10 Mn From TDK Ventures
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Delhi NCR-based cooling solutions startup Optimist is in talks to raise about $10 Mn in a fresh funding round from…
item.content:encoded:
Delhi NCR-based cooling solutions startup Optimist is in talks to raise about $10 Mn in a fresh funding round from TDK Ventures, sources told Inc42. 

TDK Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Japan’s TDK Corporation, will be a new addition to the startup’s cap table. The discussions are ongoing and the final cheque size could change before the round is closed, the sources added. 

However, Inc42 could not ascertain if the proposed investment is part of an extension of the startup’s previously announced $12 Mn seed and pre-Series A round or a separate funding round. The earlier round was led by Accel and Arkam Ventures, with participation from angel investors. 

Responding to Inc42’s queries, an Optimist spokesperson said, “At this point of time, we cannot vouch for the veracity of the mail shared with Optimist.” Questions sent to TDK Ventures didn’t elicit any response till the time of publication. 

Founded in 2024 by former Urban Ladder cofounder Ashish Goel and Pranav Chopra, Optimist builds air conditioners designed specifically for Indian conditions, where high temperatures, humidity, and electricity costs make cooling both essential and expensive. 

Speaking to Inc42 earlier this year, Goel said the startup was founded to address India’s low air-conditioner penetration. While India has more than 300 Mn households, only about 27-28 Mn own an AC even though nearly 90% of households live in regions with high heat exposure. 

“As a business, it’s a large opportunity. As a consumer-focused technologist, it’s a problem that clearly needs solving,” he said. 

Optimist operates an in-house R&D facility in Gurugram, where it has spent months researching thermodynamics, heat transfer, humidity control, and airflow optimisation to develop its products.

The startup launched its products around two months ago through its own website and Amazon, with an initial presence across Delhi NCR, Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh. It is also expanding its offline retail footprint.

The development comes as investor interest in India’s home appliance ecosystem continues to grow. Earlier this year, another new age AC startup Helium Air raised $2 Mn in a seed round from India Quotient. 

More broadly, a clutch of D2C appliance startups are betting on energy efficiency, smart connectivity, aesthetics and compact form factors to differentiate themselves in an increasingly competitive market. 

IPO-bound Atomberg, for instance, has expanded beyond its smart ceiling fans into categories such as water purifiers, mixer grinders and other kitchen appliances. Earlier this year, it also entered the B2B manufacturing segment.

item.title: PB Fintech Q1 Profit Doubles YoY To ₹163 Cr, Revenue Jumps 40%
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: PolicyBazaar parent PB Fintech’s net profit almost doubled YoY to ₹162.9 Cr in the June quarter (Q1 FY27) from ₹84.7…
item.content:encoded:
PolicyBazaar parent PB Fintech’s net profit almost doubled YoY to ₹162.9 Cr in the June quarter (Q1 FY27) from ₹84.7 Cr in the same quarter last year. 

Sequentially, the company’s PAT tumbled 38% from ₹261.2 Cr.

Operating revenue also jumped 40% YoY to ₹1,888.3 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹1,348 Cr in Q1 FY26. However, on a sequential basis, the fintech major’s top line declined 8% from ₹2,061.3 Cr in Q4 FY26.

Along with an other income of ₹93 Cr, total revenue for the quarter stood at ₹1,981.3 Cr. Total expenses for the quarter stood at ₹1,800.3 Cr, up 33% YoY.

(The story will be updated soon)

item.title: [Update] Zuckerberg Apologises Over PM Modi Video Takedown, CSAM Ads, Deepfakes
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Original | August 05, 17:27 IST   Hours after the MP Nishikant Dubey-led parliamentary panel warned Meta over its content moderation…
item.content:encoded:
Original | August 05, 17:27 IST  

Hours after the MP Nishikant Dubey-led parliamentary panel warned Meta over its content moderation practices, CEO Mark Zuckerberg has reportedly apologised for issues related to child abuse content, deepfakes and errors in platform operations.

The move came after Meta’s global team met the panel earlier in the day and later IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, as per a report by PTI. 

The government had issued summons to Meta over the brief removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook video, among other issues. The panel had also questioned Meta on content moderation, algorithmic bias, and accountability, demanding an unconditional apology from CEO Mark Zuckerberg

As per government sources , Centre told Meta team that the social media giant may not be covered under the ‘intermediary’ definition and that its safe harbour protection under the Information Technology Act could be reconsidered.

Earlier in the day, the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology sought an “unqualified apology” from Zuckerberg over the removal of PM Modi’s video and warned that Meta’s legal protections could come under review.

Original | August 05, 13:45 IST  

Meta’s regulatory scrutiny in India has intensified after the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology sought an “unqualified apology” from CEO Mark Zuckerberg over the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook video. 

The committee has also warned that Meta’s safe harbour protection under the Information Technology Act could be reconsidered. 

In a communication to MeitY, the parliamentary panel raised concerns over the removal of the video featuring PM Modi addressing students on examination controversies and paper leaks, according to ANI. 

The video remained unavailable on Facebook for nearly five to six hours before being restored by Meta.

Speaking to reporters, parliamentary panel chairperson and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey said the committee informed MeitY and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) that removing the Prime Minister’s video was beyond the role of an intermediary and amounted to acting as a publisher.

Dubey said Zuckerberg must issue an apology within three days, failing which the committee would consider recommending the withdrawal of the safe harbour protection available to social media intermediaries under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act. 

The issue was discussed during a meeting on August 3 (Monday), attended by officials from MeitY, MHA and representatives from major digital platforms, including Meta, Google, X, Snapchat and YouTube. The meeting focused on social media regulation, content moderation, and online safety.

Meta acknowledged before the committee that PM Modi’s video remained unavailable for several hours. The company had earlier attributed the incident to a technical error and restored access to the post. 

Child Safety Concerns Add To Meta’s Regulatory Challenges

Separately, the parliamentary panel directed digital platforms to take immediate action against child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and content targeting women, warning that repeated failures to remove such content could also invite action against their intermediary protections. 

This comes as the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) continues its inquiry into allegations that advertisements linked to child sexual exploitative and abuse material appeared on Meta-owned platforms. 

The child rights body issued a notice to Meta Platforms on July 3 after taking suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report on the matter. Meta submitted its response a week later, following which the NCPCR decided to examine the allegations.

The development comes alongside a separate probe initiated by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), which directed the Delhi Police to investigate allegations that paid advertisements on Instagram promoted CSAM and examine whether Meta and other entities complied with reporting obligations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

The developments add to mounting regulatory scrutiny of Meta’s platforms in India over content moderation, automated enforcement systems, child safety measures, and accountability mechanisms.

item.title: EV Startup River Mobility Bags $120 Mn To Expand Manufacturing Capacity
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Electric two-wheeler manufacturer River Mobility has raised $120 Mn (about ₹1,141 Cr) in its Series C funding round co-led by…
item.content:encoded:
Electric two-wheeler manufacturer River Mobility has raised $120 Mn (about ₹1,141 Cr) in its Series C funding round co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners and Claypond Capital. The round also saw participation from Singularity AMC, Anicut Capital, 360 ONE Asset, JIIF, and HDFC AMC, along with existing investors, including Yamaha Motor Corporation, Al Futtaim Group, and Mitsui & Co.

Notably, the round was a mix of equity and debt funding, with Elev8 contributing around $25 Mn. The debt portion saw participation from Alteria Capital, Innoven Capital, and Stride Ventures.

This was also River’s first fundraise involving Indian institutional investors. Some of its other foreign backers include Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures and Maniv Mobility, among others. 

The EV startup plans to utilise the fresh funds toward expanding its manufacturing capacity, both at the existing factory near Bengaluru and a new greenfield facility. Additionally, the funding will fuel the launch of new products in the utility lifestyle segment and help the startup in its goal of gross margin expansion and EBITDA profitability, River said in a statement. 

Founded in 2021 by Aravind Mani and Vipin George, River manufactures multiutility escooters. In 2023, it launched its first escooter, Indie, positioned as the ‘SUV for scooters’ due to its roomy exterior and ability to traverse rugged terrain. 

The startup currently operates over 75 stores across India and is targeting to expand its footprint to over 350 stores by March 2028. River has witnessed significant growth in its sales volumes in the ongoing year amid a revival of overall electric two-wheeler sales. 

In July, River saw a 24% MoM uptick in escooter registrations to 5,514 units from 4,449 in June, according to Vahan data. For context, it sold 386 units in the entire FY24. 

Prior to the current capital infusion, it had raised $68 Mn in equity funding across multiple rounds. It last raised $40 Mn from Japanese OEM Yamaha Motor Corporation. 

On the financial front, River claimed its operating revenue jumped 21X in FY25 to ₹104 Cr from ₹5 Cr in the previous fiscal year. It is yet to report its FY26 financial numbers.

item.title: Digital Arrest Scams: SC Directs RBI To Create Bank SOPs, Pushes For Victim Compensation Framework
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Amid growing instances of digital scams, the Supreme Court (SC) has directed the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to strengthen…
item.content:encoded:
Amid growing instances of digital scams, the Supreme Court (SC) has directed the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to strengthen measures against the growing threat by introducing a standard operating procedure (SOP) for banks within four weeks to deal with cyber fraud-linked accounts. 

The SOP will include a grievance redressal system, a mechanism to restore recovered money and introduce more public awareness measures, the court said, as per a report by Live Law.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued the directions while hearing suo motu proceedings on digital arrest scams.

The court also directed all states and union territories (UTs) to operationalise State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres within a month. It also asked states to adopt the e-Zero FIR mechanism in consultation with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The aim is to speed up the reporting and investigation of cyber fraud cases.

Besides, an inter-departmental committee has also been urged to look into lowering the financial threshold for CBI investigations into cyber fraud cases. The committee will examine whether multiple fraud cases linked to the same organised network can be combined for investigation.

The court noted progress made by agencies in tackling digital frauds. As per a government report, ₹18.05 Cr has been restored in 36,290 cases with the help of 57 banks and state authorities.

The latest court directions come at a time when online extortion scams are on the rise. Fraudsters often initiate conversations with unsuspecting victims, identify vulnerabilities they can exploit, and then threaten to publish defamatory content online unless they are paid.

In bid to safeguard the digital spaces, the Centre recently asked WhatsApp to introduce stronger safeguards against digital arrest scams.

The Home Ministry’s inter-departmental committee had asked the Meta-owned platform to block device IDs linked to scam activities to prevent repeat offences. The platform agreed to introduce additional safety measures, including better caller information, warnings for suspicious accounts and improved detection of impersonation attempts.

The committee also asked WhatsApp to strengthen systems to identify malicious files, misuse of government logos and AI-generated content used in scams.

The top court began examining the issue last year after a sharp rise in such frauds. It had earlier noted that more than ₹54,000 Cr had allegedly been lost through these scams and called them similar to “robbery or dacoity”.
